mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows the model to place two AuditCreated entries or two AuditDeleted entries on the same task; the injected violation forces exactly that, which AppendOnly and AuditCompleteness are designed to catch.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some t: Task | #{ ae: AuditEntry | ae.ae_task = t and ae.ae_change = AuditCreated } > 1 }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact frees PermMatrix.Allowed to be any relation; the injected violation adds MemberNonOwnerCtx -> PatchTask to Allowed, which directly contradicts FR-009 and the OwnershipBasedAccess / LeastPrivilege assertions.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_PermMatrixViolation { MemberNonOwnerCtx -> PatchTask in PermMatrix.Allowed and MemberNonOwnerCtx -> DeleteTask in PermMatrix.Allowed }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows tasks with no AuditCreated entry; the injected violation forces a task to exist with only AuditChanged entries and no AuditCreated entry, which AuditCompleteness and FR_015_AuditPerEditEvent catch.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MissingCreatedEntry { some t: Task | no ae: AuditEntry | ae.ae_task = t and ae.ae_change = AuditCreated and some ae2: AuditEntry | ae2.ae_task = t and ae2.ae_change = AuditChanged }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows ae_team to differ from task_team, creating a cross-team audit entry — exactly the information-leakage scenario FR-014 prohibits. The injection forces the mismatch.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CrossTeamAudit { some ae: AuditEntry, t2: Team | ae.ae_team != ae.ae_task.task_team and ae.ae_team = t2 }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows a task to name an assignee who is not a member of the task's team. The injected violation forces such a task to exist, which FR_012_AssigneeInSameTeam catches.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OutsideTeamAssignee { some t: Task, u: User | t.task_assignee = u and no m: TeamMembership | m.mem_user = u and m.mem_team = t.task_team }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact severs the coupling between DeletedTask membership and the presence of an AuditDeleted entry. The injection forces a DeletedTask with no AuditDeleted entry and a live Task with a spurious AuditDeleted entry, both of which AuditCompleteness catches.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_DeletedAuditMismatch { some t: DeletedTask | no ae: AuditEntry | ae.ae_task = t and ae.ae_change = AuditDeleted }
